subproblem.title: Second-order upper bound for the tangential Jacobian of I + tL when trace(P_S L) = 0
subproblem.statement:
Second-order bound for the area Jacobian. For all P ∈ ℕ and Λ ∈ ℝ there is C ∈ ℝ such that for every linear subspace S ⊆ ℝ^P, every linear map L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with operator norm ‖L‖ ≤ Λ and trace(P_S∘L) = 0, and every t ∈ ℝ with |t| ≤ 1:
 √det(((I + tL)∘ι_S)*((I + tL)∘ι_S)) ≤ 1 + (t²/2)·Σ_{j=1}^P (|L(P_Se_j) − P_S L(P_Se_j)|² − P_Se_j·L(P_S L(P_Se_j))) + C|t|³,
where P_S is the orthogonal projection onto S, ι_S : S → ℝ^P the inclusion, * the adjoint for the inner products of S and ℝ^P, det the determinant of an endomorphism of S, and e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Λ : ℝ), ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), ‖L‖ ≤ Λ → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (S.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ L.toLinearMap) = 0 → ∀ t : ℝ, |t| ≤ 1 → Real.sqrt ((((ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) + t • L).comp S.subtypeL).adjoint ∘L ((ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Euclid P) + t • L).comp S.subtypeL)).det) ≤ 1 + t ^ 2 / 2 * ∑ j : Fin P, (‖L (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)) - S.starProjection (L (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))‖ ^ 2 - inner ℝ (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)) (L (S.starProjection (L (S.starProjection (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))))) + C * |t| ^ 3
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. The Taylor expansion of J_t = √det(b(t)) in parent step (1c) (Simon Ch. 2, 5.2–5.4), for a linear map whose first-order term vanishes. Departure: instead of expanding √(1 + u) we use √y ≤ (1 + y)/2 for y ≥ 0, which is exact to second order because the first-order coefficient vanishes; no differentiation in t is needed. Dependency: det_second_order (Lean name Submission.codim1_hcp_stab_det_second_order).

Notation. ι := ι_S, T := (I + tL)∘ι : S → ℝ^P, G := T*T : S → S, u_j := P_Se_j, and Q := Σ_j (|Lu_j − P_S Lu_j|² − u_j·L(P_S Lu_j)).

1. (Constant.) Let C₁ be the constant of det_second_order for N := P and κ := 2|Λ| + Λ², and put C := max(C₁, 0)/2. Fix S, L, t as in the statement; note Λ ≥ ‖L‖ ≥ 0.

2. (Orthonormal basis; expansion of P_S.) Let n := dim S; then n ≤ P (Submodule.finrank_le). Let τ_1, …, τ_n be an orthonormal basis of S (stdOrthonormalBasis, reindexed by Fin n). For every w ∈ ℝ^P, P_S w = Σ_k (τ_k·w)τ_k: apply OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr' to the orthogonal projection π(w) ∈ S of w and use τ_k·π(w) = τ_k·w (Submodule.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_left).

3. (One trace, two bases.) For every linear R : ℝ^P → ℝ^P:
 (i) trace(P_S∘R) = Σ_j u_j·R u_j. Indeed P_S∘R = P_S∘(P_S∘R) (P_S² = P_S), so trace(P_S∘R) = trace((P_S∘R)∘P_S) (LinearMap.trace_comp_comm'), and computing this trace in the standard orthonormal basis (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with EuclideanSpace.basisFun) gives Σ_j e_j·P_S R P_S e_j = Σ_j P_Se_j·R P_Se_j (P_S self-adjoint).
 (ii) trace(P_S∘R) = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i. Indeed trace(P_S∘R) = trace(R∘P_S) and P_S = ι∘π, so (trace_comp_comm' twice) trace(P_S∘R) = trace_S(π∘R∘ι); computing the latter in the basis τ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner) gives Σ_i τ_i·π(Rτ_i) = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i.
 Consequently Σ_j u_j·R u_j = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i.   (★)

4. (Matrix of G.) In the orthonormal basis τ the (i,j) entry of G is τ_i·Gτ_j = Tτ_i·Tτ_j (definition of the adjoint) = (τ_i + tLτ_i)·(τ_j + tLτ_j) = δ_ij + tX_ij + t²Y_ij, where X_ij := τ_i·Lτ_j + Lτ_i·τ_j and Y_ij := Lτ_i·Lτ_j (orthonormality gives τ_i·τ_j = δ_ij). As the determinant of an endomorphism equals the determinant of its matrix in any basis (LinearMap.det_toMatrix), det G = det(I + tX + t²Y).

5. (Expansion.) Since |τ_i| = 1 and |Lτ_i| ≤ ‖L‖ ≤ Λ, Cauchy–Schwarz gives |X_ij| ≤ 2Λ ≤ κ and |Y_ij| ≤ Λ² ≤ κ. By det_second_order (n ≤ P, |t| ≤ 1),
 det G ≤ 1 + t·tr X + t²(tr Y + ((tr X)² − tr(X·X))/2) + C₁|t|³.

6. (First-order term.) tr X = Σ_i 2τ_i·Lτ_i = 2·trace(P_S∘L) = 0 by 3(ii) and the hypothesis.

7. (The second-order term equals Q.) Let M_ij := τ_i·Lτ_j; then X_ij = M_ij + M_ji, so tr(X·X) = Σ_{i,j}(M_ij + M_ji)² = 2Σ_{i,j}M_ij² + 2Σ_{i,j}M_ijM_ji (Σ_{i,j}M_ji² = Σ_{i,j}M_ij² by exchanging the sums), and tr Y = Σ_i|Lτ_i|². With tr X = 0 the t²-coefficient is c := Σ_i|Lτ_i|² − Σ_{i,j}M_ij² − Σ_{i,j}M_ijM_ji.
 Let R₁ := L*(I − P_S)L and R₂ := L P_S L. For every v ∈ ℝ^P: v·R₁v = Lv·(Lv − P_SLv) = |Lv − P_SLv|², because P_SLv·(Lv − P_SLv) = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_inner_eq_zero); and v·R₂v = v·L(P_SLv). Therefore, by (★),
 Q = Σ_j u_j·R₁u_j − Σ_j u_j·R₂u_j = Σ_i τ_i·R₁τ_i − Σ_i τ_i·R₂τ_i.
 By step 2, τ_i·R₁τ_i = |Lτ_i|² − Lτ_i·P_SLτ_i = |Lτ_i|² − Σ_k (τ_k·Lτ_i)² = |Lτ_i|² − Σ_k M_ki², and τ_i·R₂τ_i = τ_i·L(Σ_k (τ_k·Lτ_i)τ_k) = Σ_k M_kiM_ik. Exchanging the order of summation, Q = Σ_i|Lτ_i|² − Σ_{i,j}M_ij² − Σ_{i,j}M_ijM_ji = c.

8. (det G ≥ 0.) G is symmetric: Ga·b = Ta·Tb = a·Gb. By the spectral theorem (LinearMap.IsSymmetric.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues) det G is the product of the eigenvalues of G, and each eigenvalue λ with unit eigenvector v satisfies λ = v·Gv = |Tv|² ≥ 0. Hence det G ≥ 0.

9. (Square root.) For y ≥ 0, √y ≤ (1 + y)/2, since (√y − 1)² ≥ 0. By steps 5–7, det G ≤ 1 + t²Q + C₁|t|³ ≤ 1 + t²Q + 2C|t|³, and by step 8,
 √det G ≤ (1 + det G)/2 ≤ 1 + (t²/2)Q + C|t|³. ∎
proof_key_steps: In an orthonormal basis τ of S, det((I+tL)ι)*((I+tL)ι) = det(I + tX + t²Y) with X_ij = τ_i·Lτ_j + Lτ_i·τ_j and Y_ij = Lτ_i·Lτ_j, entries bounded by 2|Λ| + Λ².
det_second_order with tr X = 2·trace(P_S L) = 0 bounds the determinant by 1 + t²c + C₁|t|³.
The trace identity Σ_j P_Se_j·R(P_Se_j) = trace(P_S R) = Σ_i τ_i·Rτ_i, applied to L*(I−P_S)L and LP_SL, identifies c with Q.
det ≥ 0 (positive symmetric operator, spectral theorem) and √y ≤ (1+y)/2 give the bound.

audit.reason: The Gram-matrix expansion, trace-zero cancellation and change-of-basis trace identities yield exactly the stated quadratic coefficient. Positivity of the Gram determinant and √y ≤ (1+y)/2 give the bound. The constant is uniform in S and L; sum scope and subspace instances were independently checked.
